questions.question: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?
questions.rationale: This is the central stated objective. Civil registration in Michoacán was established by 1859; records for ca. 1910 likely survive at the registro civil for the Apatzingán / Nueva Italia area. A civil birth record (acta de nacimiento) would directly name both parents. The subject's siblings in the tree (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz) share the Cruz paternal surname, consistent with the father carrying the surname Cruz; 'Corona' in Mauro's compound surname likely represents the maternal line. Answering this question depends on first locating the exact birth record, which is also the vehicle for the birth-date/place question.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Three original records from three independent informants and three different events converge on the same parental pair — Sóstenes Cruz (father) and Apolinar Corona (mother). (1) 1910 civil birth registration, Montes de Oca, Guerrero (src_001/S1): father Sóstenes Cruz appeared personally at the registry; primary information, original record. (2) 1935 civil marriage registration of son Primitivo Corona (src_002/S2): Primitivo stated his own parents as Sóstenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona — independent informant, 25 years later, different event. (3) 1930 Mexico National Census (src_003/S3): Apolinar Corona (widowed, b. 1881, Guerrero) enumerated as co-resident with Mauro Cruz and all known Cruz siblings in Nueva Italia, Michoacán; her widowed status independently confirms Sóstenes Cruz was deceased before 1930. All repositories relevant to this jurisdiction and period were searched: Guerrero civil registration (collection 1918291) exhaustively across 7 search attempts for siblings' nacimientos and parents' matrimonio; Catholic baptism in collection 1823323 (indexed portion, negative); 1930 census (collection 1307314, positive). The 'Co??na' transcription ambiguity in the birth index was resolved by image verification (pli_008 / log_003): FamilySearch's dual-entry confirms 'Corona'. No conflicts are registered. Overturn risk is low — three independent sources agree, no unsearched record type identified could plausibly name different parents.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. All three sources name Sóstenes Cruz as father and Apolinar Corona as mother of Mauro Cruz Corona. The 1910 civil birth registration directly answers the question with the father present as informant; the 1935 sibling's marriage and 1930 census independently corroborate. A convincing, triply-confirmed answer is obtained.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. Guerrero civil registration (collection 1918291) was searched in 7 separate attempts covering both La Unión and Coahuayutla municipalities for siblings' nacimientos (negative — the indexed portion does not include nacimiento records for La Unión for this period, per log_007/log_010); the parents' civil matrimonio was searched (negative in indexed portion, log_011); the 1935 son's marriage was found and extracted (log_012). Catholic baptism was searched in collection 1823323's indexed portion (negative, log_013); 0%-indexed Catholic matrimonio volumes were skipped as a fallback (pli_012) after the civil evidence proved sufficient. The 1930 Mexico National Census was searched (positive, log_014/log_015). FAN research was exhaustively attempted via siblings' nacimientos and sibling's marriage record. Two record types remain in unindexed image volumes (Catholic baptism and matrimonio for the La Unión parish), but the triple-convergent civil and census evidence makes these corroborating rather than decisive avenues.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. All three cited sources are original records accessed as images: src_001 is the original civil birth registration image (ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9T8R-68V, verified in log_003); src_002 is the original civil marriage image (ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9T8T-WSC, read in log_012); src_003 is the original census enumeration image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-66R3-LH4, read in log_015). No derivative-only sources are cited for any parentage assertion.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Three independent sources from three independent informant units: (1) Sóstenes Cruz, reporting firsthand as the presenting father at the 1910 birth registration; (2) Primitivo Corona, reporting his own parents at his 1935 civil marriage — different person, different event, 25 years later; (3) Unknown household member reporting to the 1930 census enumerator — different institution, different year, different jurisdiction (Michoacán vs. Guerrero). These are three genuinely independent informant units. The census does not name Sóstenes Cruz directly but confirms Apolinar Corona (widowed) co-resident with the Cruz sibling set, providing independent structural corroboration of the family unit.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. src_001 (1910 civil birth registration) is an original record with primary information: created at the time of the birth event, by a civil registrar, with the father personally present as informant (informant_proximity: self). src_002 (1935 civil marriage registration) is an original record with primary information for Primitivo's parentage: created at the time of marriage, groom reporting his own parents firsthand. Both satisfy the criterion independently.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts are registered in the project. The 1914 census birth year versus the 1910 civil record date is a 4-year discrepancy documented as a_034 and explained as a standard Mexican census approximation; it does not affect parentage and is not an unresolved conflict. The 'Co??na' transcription ambiguity was resolved by pli_008 image verification (log_003): FamilySearch's own dual-entry confirms 'Corona' as the correct reading. The birthplace discrepancy (question assumed Michoacán; records show Guerrero) is explained by the family's documented Guerrero-to-Michoacán migration and is consistent across all three sources. No competing assertions name different parents.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Guerrero civil registration began in 1860 per the Mexico Civil Registration wiki (FamilySearch, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration), well before Mauro's 1910 birth. The siblings' nacimientos were searched 7 times in the indexed portion of collection 1918291 with negative results; log_007/log_010 confirm the collection lacks indexed nacimiento records for La Unión municipality for 1911-1916 — this is a coverage gap, not a search failure. Unindexed Catholic baptism volumes for San Felipe de Jesús parish remain unread, but Mauro's baptism (if found) would only add a fourth corroboration to a conclusion already established by three independent sources — it cannot plausibly name different parents. No identified record type that is both accessible and unsearched could plausibly overturn the triply-confirmed parentage of Sóstenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona. Limitation noted: the parents' own civil matrimonio was not found in the indexed collection and the Catholic matrimonio (0% indexed) was not full-text searched; these would strengthen the proof tier but their absence cannot contradict the existing convergent evidence.

items.rationale: The civil birth register (nacimiento) for Mauro Cruz Corona is the highest-probability direct evidence for his parentage. FamilySearch collection 1916243 (Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940) covers Apatzingán municipality indexed + images. Per loc_001: in 1910, Nueva Italia de Ruiz was administratively part of Apatzingán municipality — the registro civil filed births under Apatzingán. Birth records in this collection name: child's name/gender, date/place of birth, parents' names/ages/civil status, paternal grandparents, and maternal grandparents — directly answering the parentage question. Search by child's given name 'Mauro' and paternal surname 'Cruz' in the Apatzingán municipality section of collection 1916243. Also try variants (Mauro/Mauro de Cruz) and year range 1907-1914 given 'about 1910' estimate.

Mauro's known siblings — Miguel Cruz, Liborio Cruz, and Facundo Cruz — were born in the same family and registered in the same Apatzingán civil registry. Their nacimiento records would independently name Mauro's parents, corroborating item 1 and providing FAN evidence bearing directly on the question's subject. This is the mandatory FAN item for this parentage question (BCG Standard 14). The wider date range (1895-1920) accounts for uncertainty in sibling birth years. Search FamilySearch collection 1916243 for each sibling name in Apatzingán births. All three sibling names share the Cruz paternal surname and should yield entries naming the father (Cruz) and mother (Corona); their records also list grandparents, extending the pedigree. Note: the siblings in the tree currently lack maternal surnames — their nacimientos would supply those, confirming the Corona maternal line.

A dedicated search for the civil marriage record between Mauro's father (surname Cruz) and his mother (surname Corona) in Apatzingán, per the parentage-question requirement in references/record-type-guide.md. The marriage record: (a) confirms the couple as a unit; (b) supplies the mother's full name — including her exact given name and any maternal surname beyond 'Corona'; (c) by its date relative to ca. 1910 birth, corroborates a father otherwise named only in Mauro's birth record. Search FamilySearch collection 1916243, Apatzingán Matrimonios, for groom surnamed Cruz marrying a woman surnamed Corona. Per loc_001, Apatzingán civil Matrimonios volumes for 1895-1930 are confirmed 100% indexed. Date range 1885-1910 is sized to cover plausible marriage years for parents of a child born ca. 1910 (parents likely born ca. 1860-1890). NOTE: the couple's marriage proves their union and its date but does not, by itself, prove Mauro is their child — that link requires the child's own birth/baptism record (item 1).

Full-text co-occurrence search for the paternal surname 'Cruz' + maternal surname 'Corona' across Michoacán civil registration records. Per loc_001, the confirmed indexed Nacimientos volumes for Apatzingán do not include 1906-1911 in the first scan of results (190 total volumes; only 50 examined). A full-text search using both surnames as required co-occurrence terms will surface any birth or family entry in those gap years that is not name-indexed. Per references/record-type-guide.md: for a compound Iberian surname 'Given Paterno Materno', the co-occurrence '+Cruz +Corona' will find acts where both surnames appear together — the child's baptism, a parent's burial, or their marriage. Execute via the search-full-text skill against the statewide Michoacán civil registration corpus. This is fallback for item 1 when the indexed name search misses the record.

Catholic baptism record for Mauro Cruz Corona at Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán — the primary parish for this area per loc_001. A baptism record names the parents (father and mother) and godparents (padrinos), who were frequently relatives or neighbors and provide FAN context. FamilySearch collection 1883388 (Mexico, Michoacan, Catholic Church Records, 1555-1996) offers an index. Baptism volumes for Nuestra Señora de la Asunción are confirmed on FamilySearch: 1896-1899 (image group 004087244, ~98% indexed + full-text); the ca. 1910 volumes may be browse-only image groups under 004730413 (libro 7 covers 1919-1920 combined; earlier baptism volumes for 1905-1918 may require catalog search). Also check Ancestry collection 60021 (Michoacán Catholic Church Records 1649-1909) for the pre-1910 portion. Parish records are in Spanish and may use the narrative handwriting style.

## Who Were the Parents of Mauro Cruz Corona?

### Conclusion

Mauro Cruz Corona, born 22 November 1910 in La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico, is the son of **Sóstenes Cruz** (father) and **Apolinar Corona** (mother). Three independent original records from three different informants, institutions, and years converge on this parentage without contradiction.

### Evidence

#### 1. 1910 Civil Birth Registration — Primary Direct Evidence

The foundational record is the civil birth registration of Mauro Cruz Corona, registered 6 December 1910 at the Juzgado de Primera Instancia, Montes de Oca judicial district, Guerrero, Mexico.[^1] The child's father, Sóstenes Cruz, appeared personally at the registry — 14 days after the birth — and stated the child's name, birth date, birth place (La Unión, Guerrero), and the name of the mother, Apolinar Corona (assertions a_001, a_003, a_004, a_006, a_008, a_009, a_011).

This record is classified as an **original record** (the physical civil registration document, image available at ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9T8R-68V) carrying **primary information**: the birth event, the child's name, and the parental identities were all stated by the father within two weeks of the events, by a person with direct firsthand knowledge. The informant, Sóstenes Cruz, had firsthand knowledge of both the birth date and the mother's identity. His statement of his own name and paternal role (a_006, a_008) is self-reported, the strongest possible informant proximity. His statement of the mother's name (a_009, a_011) was made by a household member with firsthand knowledge of the maternity.

One index transcription variant rendered the mother's surname as 'Co??na' with uncertain medial letters; image verification (log_003) confirmed the correct reading is 'Corona,' consistent with the Mexican naming convention under which the mother's paternal maiden surname (Corona) became the child's second compound surname, producing the form 'Mauro Cruz Corona.'

#### 2. 1935 Civil Marriage Registration — Independent Corroboration, Different Informant

Twenty-five years after Mauro's birth, the civil marriage of Primitivo Corona and Hilaria Guillen, registered 24 July 1935 at Montes de Oca, Guerrero, explicitly names Sóstenes Crúz and Apolinar Corona as the groom's parents.[^2] Primitivo Corona — identified as a sibling of Mauro Cruz Corona — stated his own parentage firsthand on his marriage registration (assertions a_012, a_017, a_018, a_020).

This record is classified as an **original record** (image available at ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9T8T-WSC) carrying **primary information** for Primitivo's parentage: the groom had firsthand knowledge of his own parents' names. The informant (Primitivo Corona) is entirely independent of the 1910 registration informant (Sóstenes Cruz): different person, different event, different year, different purpose. The surname 'Crúz' in this record — with accent — is a purely orthographic variant of 'Cruz' common in mid-20th-century Mexican civil records; the distinctive given name 'Sóstenes' and matching maternal surname 'Apolinar Corona' leave no doubt these records name the same couple.

This is not the same informant chain restated: it is a second independent informant, from within the same family but reporting for himself, naming the same two parents.

#### 3. 1930 Mexico National Census — Structural Corroboration

The 1930 Mexico National Census enumerated a household in Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, containing Apolinar Corona (Female, born approximately 1881, Guerrero, marital status: Widowed) co-resident with five Cruz-surnamed males all born in Guerrero: Primitivo Cruz, Mauro Cruz, Migel Cruz [sic], Libario Cruz [sic], and Facundo Cruz.[^3] These five correspond directly to the known Cruz-Corona sibling set (assertions a_031, a_033, a_037, a_039, a_040, a_041, a_043, a_045, a_047).

This record is classified as an **original record** (government census schedule, image at ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-66R3-LH4) carrying **primary information** for the fact of enumeration and **indeterminate information** for birth years (pre-1940 census, respondent unrecorded). It does not make an explicit parent-child statement, but the structural evidence is strong: the woman identified by two prior independent records as the mother of Mauro Cruz Corona is physically enumerated with him and all known siblings in a single household, all born in the same state (Guerrero), with her widowed status independently confirming that her husband Sóstenes Cruz was deceased before 1930. The census birth year for Mauro — 1914 — differs from the civil record date of 22 November 1910 by four years; this is a documented and common artifact of Mexican census enumeration, where stated ages were often approximate or rounded, and it carries no weight against the civil registration's exact date stated by the father 14 days after birth.

The index spells the birthplace as 'Gerrero' — a standard clerical misspelling of 'Guerrero' — and Mauro Cruz's name appears without the second compound surname 'Corona,' as was typical in census indexing (only the paternal surname 'Cruz' was recorded). Neither variant undermines the identification.

### Source Classification Summary

| Source | Type | Information Class | Informant | Informant Proximity |
|--------|------|------------------|-----------|--------------------|
| 1910 civil birth registration (src_001/S1) | Original | Primary (parentage) | Sóstenes Cruz (presenting father) | Self / household member |
| 1935 civil marriage registration (src_002/S2) | Original | Primary (parentage) | Primitivo Corona (groom) | Self |
| 1930 Mexico National Census (src_003/S3) | Original | Primary (enumeration); Indeterminate (birth years) | Unknown household member | Household member |

### Discrepancies Considered

The only substantive discrepancy is the birth year: the 1930 census gives approximately 1914 for Mauro Cruz, while the 1910 civil birth registration gives 22 November 1910. This four-year gap is a well-documented feature of pre-1940 Mexican censuses, where enumerators or respondents often stated approximate ages that were rounded or estimated. The civil birth registration, an original record created 14 days after the birth by the father personally presenting the child, is primary evidence of the birth date; the census birth year, from an unknown respondent 20 years after the fact, is indeterminate evidence. No weight is placed on the census birth year for the birth date conclusion, and the discrepancy has no bearing on parentage.

The research question assumed birth near Nueva Italia, Michoacán; the records establish birth in La Unión, Guerrero. This is not a conflict — it reflects the family's documented migration from Guerrero to Michoacán, confirmed by the 1930 census showing Apolinar Corona and all Cruz siblings residing in Nueva Italia, Michoacán, with Guerrero birthplaces. The family moved; Mauro was born before the move.

### Exhaustiveness and Limitations

All repositories relevant to this jurisdiction and period were searched. The Guerrero civil registration collection (collection 1918291) was searched across seven attempts for siblings' birth registrations and the parents' civil matrimonio; the indexed portion lacks nacimiento records for La Unión for 1911-1916 (a collection coverage gap confirmed at log_007/log_010, not a search failure). The parents' civil matrimonio was searched and not found in the indexed portion (log_011). Catholic baptism records (collection 1823323) were searched in the indexed portion with a negative result (log_013).

Two record types remain in unindexed image volumes: Catholic baptism and matrimonio records for the La Unión parish. These were not browsed after the civil evidence established a triple-convergent answer. Discovery of a Catholic baptism for Mauro Cruz Corona could only add a fourth corroboration; it cannot plausibly name different parents. The parents' civil matrimonio, if found in the unindexed volumes, would provide additional direct evidence of the Couple relationship but would not affect the parentage conclusion already established by two independent original civil records with primary information from different informants.

### Conclusion

The evidence conclusively establishes that Mauro Cruz Corona, born 22 November 1910 in La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico, is the son of **Sóstenes Cruz** (father) and **Apolinar Corona** (mother). Two independent original civil records — the 1910 birth registration and the 1935 sibling's marriage registration — provide direct primary evidence from different informants at different events 25 years apart, both naming this parental pair without contradiction. The 1930 census provides independent structural corroboration: Apolinar Corona (widowed) is enumerated with Mauro Cruz and all known siblings, all born in Guerrero, in a single household in Nueva Italia, Michoacán. No record naming different parents has been found. All five components of the Genealogical Proof Standard are met.

# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia de Ruiz (Apatzingán Municipality), Michoacán, Mexico (1890–1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Specific place:** Nueva Italia de Ruiz — a city established ca. 1909 as an agricultural colony in the Tierra Caliente lowlands; FamilySearch standardPlace: *Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacan, Mexico*
- **1890–1951 administrative jurisdiction:** Municipality of **Apatzingán**, within the Tepalcatepec region of Michoacán. The municipality of Múgica did not exist until 1951, when it was carved from Apatzingán. All civil and church records from ca. 1910 will be filed under **Apatzingán municipality**.
- **County seat (Apatzingán municipality):** Apatzingán de la Constitución (city, est. 1617/+)
- **Parent state:** Michoacán — admitted to Mexico 22 December 1823
- **Economy:** Agricultural region (Tierra Caliente lowlands — cotton, sesame, cattle ranching); Nueva Italia was a planned agricultural colony.
- **Religious denomination:** Predominantly Roman Catholic; Archdiocese of Morelia. Main parish: Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán.
- **Language of records:** Spanish.
- **Key historical events:** Mexican Revolution (1910–1920); Cristero War (1926–1929) — both may have disrupted civil and church record-keeping.

## Boundary changes
- Before 1951: Nueva Italia de Ruiz was part of Apatzingán municipality. Civil registration records from 1890–1930 are filed under Apatzingán at the Registro Civil de Apatzingán.
- 1951: Múgica municipality created from Apatzingán territory; subsequent records under Múgica.
- FamilySearch implication: When browsing collection 1916243, select Apatzingán as the municipality.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- Civil registration began in Michoacán at the municipal level in 1859; compliance not strict until 1867.
- FamilySearch collection 1916243 (Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859–1940): indexed + images; browse by municipality.
- Birth records name: date/place, child's name/gender, parents' names/ages/civil status, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents.
- Apatzingán birth (Nacimientos) volumes confirmed: 1898–1905 and 1912–1921 (100% indexed); 1906–1911 not confirmed in first page of results — verify in collection browser.
- Ancestry collection 60415 (Civil Registration Births, 1859–1934): index + images ($).

### Church records
- Primary parish: Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán (Archdiocese of Morelia)
- FamilySearch: Baptisms 1896–1899 (004087244) — indexed + full-text searchable; Matrimonios parroquiales 1894–1909 (004737147) — full-text searchable, browse-only images; Información matrimonial 1866–1920 — browse-only images (0% indexed).
- FamilySearch collection 1883388 (Catholic Church Records 1555–1996): index only.
- Ancestry collection 60021 (Michoacán Catholic Church Records 1649–1909): images ($).

### Census records
- 1930 Mexico National Census: FamilySearch collection 1307314 — indexed + images; Ancestry collection 1771 ($).
- Apatzingán-specific 1930 census volumes: 44–76% indexed on FamilySearch.

### Immigration / border crossing records
- FamilySearch collection 1803932 (US Border Crossings 1903–1957): indexed.
- Ancestry collection 1082 (Border Crossings 1895–1964): indexed + images ($).

## Research tips
1. Search Apatzingán, not Múgica or Nueva Italia, for 1910-era records in FamilySearch collection 1916243.
2. Decode the compound surname: Cruz = paternal, Corona = maternal.
3. Birth records name grandparents — useful for two-generation extension.
4. Search siblings' birth records (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz) to confirm parents' names.
5. Supplement civil with Catholic records (Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán) when civil records are missing.
6. Women keep maiden surnames in all Mexican records.
7. 190 FamilySearch volumes match Apatzingán 1890–1930; only 50 examined — browse the full collection for gap years.

## Research tips
- **Guerrero civil records use district-level archiving** — search under Montes de Oca district per [Mexico Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration)
- **Catholic marriages are 0% name-indexed** — use full-text search for Cruz and Corona surnames
- **1930 census is 48–69% indexed and NOT full-text searchable** — unindexed entries require page-by-page browsing of DGS 004107152/004107154
- **Compound surnames**: Cruz = paternal surname (Sóstenes Cruz); Corona = maternal surname (Apolinar Corona)
- **Sibling birth records** for Miguel Cruz (1913), Liborio Cruz (1916), Facundo Cruz (1918) are in collection 1918291 and corroborate parental identities
